name: Marta Ellingsen
summary: Widow of the Skarvik lighthouse keeper. Kept the lamp after his death without appointment or pay. No dependants living; two foster children, grown.

entries.text: Kept the Skarvik light burning 31 years after her husband died, unpaid, unasked.
Took in two children orphaned by the wreck of the Solveig; raised them as hers.
Stole coal from the harbour store during the winter of 1941.
Refused to speak to her sister for forty years over an inheritance of six spoons.
Attended no place of worship after 1923.

archive.title: Records note: Skarvik
cards: Harbour board minutes, 1923-54: 'the light shown nightly; keeper unpaid.'
Parish register: the Solveig lost 1925; two infants placed with Mrs Ellingsen.
Slip in Pell's hand: 'Nothing contradicts the file. Filed as read. O.P.'

questions.text: Why keep the light when nobody paid you?
answer: Boats don't stop coming because a man dies. Somebody had to go up the stairs. I had the knees for it then.
questions.card: Kept the light because boats kept coming and somebody had to climb.

answer: The lamp room was freezing and the oil was thick as porridge. I took four sacks. I'd take five, knowing what I know.
questions.card: Took four sacks of coal so the lamp oil stayed thin enough to burn.

fact.text: The stolen coal kept the Skarvik lamp burning through the winter of 1941.

answer: They were Mother's spoons and she knew it. ...Is she here? No, don't tell me. Yes, tell me.
questions.card: Still sure the spoons were hers. Wants news of her sister, then doesn't.

heaven: She asks whether there are stairs. Told there are none, she looks faintly disappointed.
hell: The Wardens return her file within the day, marked "Sent in error?"
Marrow leaves it on your desk without comment.

ext.teaches: Walk, call, read, stamp, door, slip
ext.mitigating: The coal kept the light working; the theft served the virtue.
